summary: Sidereal Confluence is built almost entirely around a frantic, simultaneous live-trading phase where every player scrambles to strike deals for the exact resource cubes their race's economy needs, followed by a quick simultaneous conversion/scoring phase. It rewards social skill, reading who needs what, and building a self-sufficient engine, more than any kind of tactical board-level play.
praised: Electric, high-energy free-form trading phase unlike almost any other game
Strong asymmetry between the alien races creates very different strategies each game
Low downtime for a big-box game since everyone trades at once
Satisfying engine-building feel as your economy compounds turn to turn
criticised: Chaotic and can be overwhelming or intimidating for shy or less assertive players
Needs a near-full table (ideally 6-8) to sing; feels flat at low counts
Real-time trading can let louder/more experienced players dominate deals
Fiddly bookkeeping with lots of cubes, cards, and races to track

scoring.why: Points come from a mix of converted resources, technologies researched, and race-specific bonuses, so whoever builds the most efficient trading-fueled economy over the rounds wins.
